role: calibration only: Siegel-zero scenario, i.e. would a tiny L(1,χ_{−4p}) starve Type II / (★)?
missing_theorem: (Answered at main-term level.) It cannot starve the (★) main term. M_BM = M₀ − T with T ∝ L(1,χ_p)² (BM_LVALUE Thm A), and unconditionally M_BM(p) ≥ 0.9225·M₀(p) at p ≡ 1 (8) and ≥ M₀ − o(1) at p ≡ 5 (8) (Stephens). A Siegel discriminant −4p only changes small-prime residue patterns. Apparent h(−4p) effects among (★)-zeros are the p ≡ 1 (3) conditioning artefact (out_Q06 Z0803). Fluctuations below the main term are the open part (H⁻_BM).
status_ref: BM_LVALUE.md Thm A + 0.9225·M₀ bound; out_Q06 Z0803 (scripts/z52d_avenue_Q06_hzeros.py); BRAINSTORM/hardness_law.md
note: The 'starvation' claim is false at main-term level, unconditionally.

role: calibration only: residual correlation between consecutive primes ≡ 1 (4)
missing_theorem: (Calibration; null.) Pass 1: lag-1 correlation +0.02 after size detrending and class-mod-840 removal (the item's −0.09 was not reproduced). Privacy of large primes predicts independence beyond shared small-prime classes.

role: calibration only: Kloosterman sums K(1,1;p) vs ES counts (null test)
missing_theorem: (Calibration; null as expected.) Spearman −0.009 (n = 1125, p ≤ 2·10⁴). K(1,1;p) is a complete sum at modulus p, while ES counts are incomplete, height-dependent sub-counts of the modular hyperbola (§7.1).

role: calibration only: products of consecutive odd primes (105, 15015) as zeros of word families
missing_theorem: (Calibration.) Sub-route zeros at n = 3·5·7, 3·5·7·11·13 are 'lost lines': small prime factors of n kill the words whose parameters must be coprime to n (cf. FRONTIER §7.14, 3985). ES at composites follows from any prime factor by scaling. Pass 1: R(105) = 0, R(15015) = 0 (K-truncated), R(385) = 4.

role: calibration only: Σ_{p≤N} f(p)/(N log²N) decreasing to ≈ 0.75 (order N log²N, no log log N)
missing_theorem: (Known, internally.) The data favour order N log²N, and this is now an internal theorem for Type I: Σ_{p≤N} f_I(p) ≪ N log²N unconditionally ((D)32b, PROVED relative to Kuznetsov/Petersson, Weil, Selberg 3/16; needs external scrutiny). This removes ET's log log N. The slow decrease is a lower-order term (c + d/log N). Average statement (B6).

role: calibration only: Σ_{n≤N} f(n) over all n outgrows N log³N
missing_theorem: (Calibration; heuristic explanation.) Over composites, f(n) includes solutions inherited from every divisor d | n by scaling, so Σ_{n≤N} f(n) ≳ Σ_d f_{I,II}(d)·N/d ≈ N Σ_d log³d/d ≍ N log⁴N heuristically. A growing ratio to N log³N is then expected. ET's log³ average refers to Type I/II-type counts. No proof role.
status_ref: FRONTIER §1 Counts (ET: average of f(n) ≍ log³n, which needs the precise definition of f); Pass 1 U03
next: Check ET's exact definition of f(n) for composite n before fitting. If it includes inherited solutions, the log exponent should be 4.

role: calibration only: least prime ≡ 1 (mod p) vs ES counts (null cross-check)
missing_theorem: (Calibration; null.) Pass 1: the raw Spearman of 0.17 is a size effect, and the partial correlation on log p is −0.04. Primes in progressions mod p carry no information on divisor classes of p-tied integers mod 4C.

role: divisor switching with a moving modulus (d ↔ N/d)
missing_theorem: (Known, trivial.) For N = 4Cp+1 ≡ 1 (mod 4C), d ↦ N/d preserves the class −1, so R(p) = 2·#{d < √N certifying}. That is FRONTIER §2.1's divisor form. As an exceptional-set device, 'divisor switching' is among the capped CRT architectures (BREADTH_Z45 §15).
status_ref: FRONTIER §2.1 divisor form; §6 'divisor switching … → capped' (BREADTH_Z45 §15); Pass 1 U03 (covered)

role: calibration only: clustering of low-count primes in progressions / short intervals
missing_theorem: (Calibration.) Pass 1: bottom-decile membership is flat mod 8 (0.107–0.120). Expected structure: RESIDUE_HARDNESS's local factor (class 1 mod q is hardest, mod 840 class 1 hardest of 96) and no short-interval clustering (privacy). Main term only.

role: smooth auxiliary values: pick C with 4Cp+1 smooth and let many small prime classes cover −1 (Davenport/Erdős–Rényi template)
missing_theorem: For every p there is C ≤ X(p) such that 4Cp+1 is y-smooth and its prime-factor classes in (ℤ/4C)^× have −1 among their subset products. Smoothness raises the success rate (Pass 1: ×4, through more divisors). But no number of prime factors forces −1: all primes ≡ 1 (mod 4C) is always possible, and Davenport/Olson constants force the product 1, not −1. So the class condition (B2) survives intact. Davenport forcing is a recorded board dead end.
status_ref: FRONTIER §6 'Boards: Davenport forcing … → refuted or a restatement'; (J)57 (2-adic/Fano forcing only for M ∈ {2,3,4}); Pass 1 U03

role: calibration only: rough–smooth partition of auxiliary values
missing_theorem: (Calibration.) Pass 1: success falls monotonically with log P⁺/log N (0.121 → 0.004), as divisor counts predict. No complementary construction emerges.

role: family selection as a Frobenius condition in a fixed finite extension
missing_theorem: A selector choosing which ET family certifies p is a Chebotarev (Frobenius) condition in a fixed finite Galois extension, and the selected families always succeed. This is false: fixed finite Frobenius data are inert on finite witness sets ((J)96), and any bounded procedure fails i.o. under H (B1 Thm C). Pass 1 found only the known mod-840 class effect.
status_ref: FRONTIER §3 B1 (Thm C) and (J)96; CLASS_FORCING Thm 2.1; Pass 1 U03

role: calibration only: pretentious-character diagnostics of stubborn divisor-residue biases
missing_theorem: (Known in kind.) The sterile (square-mimicking) points are exactly where χ_p 'pretends' to be trivial on all small primes (B1 Thm M's profinite point). Measured biases at actual primes are the RESIDUE_HARDNESS/BM main-term characters. A pretentious-distance diagnostic re-measures these.
status_ref: POINTWISE_SIZE Thm M (square-mimicking point); BRAINSTORM/bsB_sterile_pretentious.md; RESIDUE_HARDNESS.md

role: Bohr-set (simultaneous fractional-part) windows for parametrisation conditions
missing_theorem: For every p some (u,B) has {p/(4uB)} = {−(u+B)/(4uB)}, i.e. the pair form of (★) as a Bohr-type window. Restatement (circular). The window depends on the height (tied), so Bohr-set density arguments (which need a fixed frequency set and power-size sets) do not apply.
